# Grammi

> Grammi is a free calorie counter app for iPhone (with an Apple Watch app), in 13 languages. Barcode scanning with no daily limit
> and the food diary are free for good. No ads, no account; the diary stays on the iPhone. Grammi Pro is an optional subscription.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6815835582?pt=129503653&ct=llms&mt=8

## Facts
- **Is Grammi free?** Yes. Barcode scanning with no daily limit and logging every meal (search, manual entry, daily totals) are free for good, along with goals, weight and water. Grammi Pro is optional: meal photos, an adapted calorie target, 30- and 90-day charts and a fasting timer, with a 7-day free trial.
- **Does Grammi have ads?** No. There are no ads in Grammi, on the free plan or on Pro.
- **Do I need an account?** No. Open the app and start logging. Your food diary is stored on your iPhone, not in an account.
- **Can I bring my history from another app?** Yes. Export a CSV file from your previous app and import it into Grammi; meals and weigh-ins keep their dates.
- **Is there a calorie counter app with a game?** Yes: Grammi has two free daily food games. In Calorie sense, everyone gets the same 5 foods and guesses their calories from 4 options; in Plate sort, you sort 12 foods into 4 hidden groups. Play them in the app, on a Home Screen widget or in your browser: https://grammiapp.com/game/ and https://grammiapp.com/plate-sort/. You can also challenge a friend with a link.
- **Does Grammi have widgets?** Yes. Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets show the calories left today in the colour and counter look you picked in the app, and a game widget lets you play the daily calorie game from the Home Screen. Control Center buttons add water, open the barcode scanner or open the game. All of this is free; with Pro, widget buttons add water or repeat a meal, and a Lock Screen countdown shows your fast.
- **Can I track GLP-1 medication like Ozempic® or Mounjaro®?** Yes. Grammi logs your GLP-1 doses (semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide), suggests the next injection site and keeps a two-tap daily note on appetite, nausea and constipation, right next to your food diary, with an optional dose-day reminder. Logging is free, needs no account and stays on your iPhone; the chart of appetite after each dose is part of Grammi Pro. Grammi keeps a log only: it doesn't give medical advice or suggest doses.
- **Does Grammi work on iPhone Duo?** Yes. Grammi fills the whole screen on iPhone Duo, both the outer display and the 7.6-inch inner display, and its screens resize when you fold or unfold the phone.
- **Which devices and languages?** Grammi is an iPhone app with an Apple Watch app, available in 13 languages.

## Features (as in the App Store listing)
Free, for good:
- Unlimited barcode scanning, backed by the Open Food Facts database of millions of products
- Not in the database? Photograph the nutrition label. Grammi reads the numbers, you check them, and the product is remembered for next time
- Basic foods — eggs, fruit, rice, meat — with real portion sizes, in your language, even offline
- Search, add food by hand, copy yesterday's meals
- Calories, protein, carbs and fat — plus fiber, sugar, saturated fat and sodium
- Daily goals, a weight log with a 7-day average, water and streaks
- Every chart for the last 7 days
- Widgets in your colour and counter look, Control Center buttons, Apple Watch, Siri Shortcuts and Apple Health
- Export your diary as a spreadsheet (CSV) — it's your data
- GLP-1 medication log for semaglutide, tirzepatide or liraglutide: a dose-day reminder, injection-site rotation and a two-tap daily note on appetite and side effects — a log only, never dose advice
- Plants & fiber: a weekly card with how many different plants you ate, plus fiber and protein
- Badges for logging, streaks, protein, water and more — Bronze is free
- Two daily food games, also on your Home Screen: Calorie sense (guess the calories) and Plate sort (12 foods, 4 hidden groups). Challenge friends, keep your streak with shields, and get a recap of your year every December
- On iPhones with Apple Intelligence (iPhone 15 Pro or newer, iOS 26): recipes written for your goal, with nutrition calculated from the food database, not guessed

Grammi Pro (optional: a monthly or yearly subscription with a 7-day free trial, or a one-time lifetime purchase):
- An adaptive target: your real burn rate, calculated from what you ate and how your weight actually moved — not a formula based on your age
- Weekly challenges, personal records and Streak run: rounds of 5 back to back, counting your perfect rounds and correct answers in a row
- 30- and 90-day charts, plus a chart builder
- Fasting timer and Ramadan mode: suhoor and iftar times calculated on your phone, offline
- Macro planner with separate targets for training and rest days
- Import recipes from a link and log food by voice
- Vitamin and mineral report, suggestions for what fits the rest of your day, and app icons
- Photograph a meal (iPhone 15 Pro or newer, iOS 27)
- GLP-1 insights: your appetite on each day after a dose, and your weight with every dose change marked
- Four more looks for the calorie counter: a fuel gauge, a plate of where your calories came from, 200-calorie bites and calories by meal
- Widget buttons to add water or repeat a meal, and an iftar countdown on the Lock Screen
- Plants & fiber over 30 and 90 days, and illustrated covers for recipes without a photo
- Badges up to Diamond, a meal plan with a shopping list, and private progress photos
- Family Sharing: one Yearly or Lifetime purchase covers up to six family members

iPhone Duo: Yes. Grammi fills the whole screen on iPhone Duo, both the outer display and the 7.6-inch inner display, and its screens resize when you fold or unfold the phone.

## Guides
- [Free calorie app for iPhone with no ads and no account](https://grammiapp.com/guides/free-calorie-counter-iphone-no-ads-no-account.html): What to check before you pick a free calorie counter for iPhone: daily logging limits, barcode limits, ads, sign-up and where your data is stored. And how Grammi handles each.
- [How to count calories for free](https://grammiapp.com/guides/how-to-count-calories-for-free.html): A simple step-by-step method to count calories for free: set a daily target, log every meal, use real portions, scan barcodes, weigh food once and review your week.
- [How to count calories when eating out](https://grammiapp.com/guides/count-calories-eating-out.html): Restaurant meals have no label. How to estimate the portion, log the main parts, allow for oil and sauces, and use typical restaurant portions to count calories when eating out.
- [How to log food that has no barcode or isn’t in the database](https://grammiapp.com/guides/log-food-without-barcode.html): Loose produce, bakery items, home cooking and products the database doesn’t know: three ways to log them in a calorie counter, and how Grammi handles each.
- [How to move your food diary to a new calorie app](https://grammiapp.com/guides/move-food-diary-to-new-calorie-app.html): Switching calorie counters without losing your history: export a CSV from your old app and import it into Grammi. Meals and weigh-ins keep their dates.
- [Calorie counter app with a game: train your eye for portion sizes](https://grammiapp.com/guides/calorie-counter-app-with-game.html): Grammi’s daily calorie guessing game: the same 5 foods for everyone, 4 answers each. A quick way to learn what a portion is worth, free in the app and in your browser.
- [Track your GLP-1 shots and what you eat, free and with no account](https://grammiapp.com/guides/track-glp1-ozempic-mounjaro-doses-free.html): How to log Ozempic®, Wegovy®, Mounjaro® or Zepbound® doses, rotate injection sites, note appetite and side effects, and keep an eye on protein, all in one free iPhone app with no account.
- [Calorie counter with badges, streaks and a meal plan](https://grammiapp.com/guides/calorie-counter-with-badges-and-meal-plan.html): Badges for logging, streaks, protein and water, a weekly page of what went well, and a meal plan with a shopping list: how they keep you counting, and what is free in Grammi.
- [Calorie counter widget for iPhone, in your colour](https://grammiapp.com/guides/calorie-counter-widget-iphone.html): How to put your calories on the iPhone Home Screen, Lock Screen and Control Center with Grammi’s widgets: what each one shows, how to play the daily food game from a widget, and what is free.
- [Daily food puzzle: sort 12 foods into 4 hidden groups](https://grammiapp.com/guides/daily-food-puzzle-plate-sort.html): Plate sort is a free daily food puzzle from Grammi: 12 foods, 4 hidden groups of 3, four mistakes allowed. How to play, what the groups mean and how it sharpens your sense of calories.
- Other languages: [Español](https://grammiapp.com/es/guias/) · [Deutsch](https://grammiapp.com/de/ratgeber/) · [Français](https://grammiapp.com/fr/guides/) · [Italiano](https://grammiapp.com/it/guide/) · [Português (Brasil)](https://grammiapp.com/pt-br/guias/) · [Türkçe](https://grammiapp.com/tr/rehberler/) · [日本語](https://grammiapp.com/ja/guides/) · [한국어](https://grammiapp.com/ko/guides/) · [Bahasa Indonesia](https://grammiapp.com/id/panduan/) · [Русский](https://grammiapp.com/ru/guides/) · [العربية](https://grammiapp.com/ar/guides/)
